description: We are CS students passionate about AI and space safety, tackling the "Flame in Freefall" challenge. Our mission is to apply machine learning to microgravity combustion data to predict fire risks and protect astronauts. We're looking for teammates with skills in Python, ML, data engineering, frontend, or research. If you want to build something meaningful, join us!
summary:
Fire in microgravity behaves counterintuitively: without buoyancy, flames form stealth spherical domes and nanoscale smoke evades conventional detectors. Crucial NASA combustion data has remained fragmented across disparate archives.

Team Astro_Sapien developed IGNIS-G (FIRELINE), an autonomous spacecraft fire-safety intelligence operating system. Unifying Grounded Gemini 2.5 Flash RAG and a LangChain SQL Agent over 1,077 flight runs and 6,287 measurements, it guarantees 0% hallucination across any space dataset. The platform features hands-free Voice AI CapCom, OpenCV smoke plume surveillance, and an interactive Simulation Lab with FLIR thermal imaging.

IGNIS-G solves the challenge by providing instant, evidence-grounded fire protection intelligence, ensuring mission-critical life-support safety for astronaut crews across the ISS, Artemis Lunar Base, and deep-space Mars expeditions.
details:
1. WHAT DOES IT DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?

IGNIS-G (FIRELINE) is an autonomous spacecraft fire-safety intelligence operating system that unifies six decades of fragmented microgravity combustion research into an interactive, zero-hallucination decision-support engine.

The platform operates across four integrated layers: • NASA Evidence Core: Ingests and standardizes data from 5 premier NASA microgravity combustion investigations (BASS-II, SAME-R, SAFFIRE-I/II/IV, FLEX/FLEX-2, SPICE), structuring 1,077 normalized flight test runs, 6,287 measurement points, and 662 indexed technical report chunks into a live Supabase PostgreSQL database. • Dual-Engine Deterministic AI: Combines a LangChain Conversational SQL Agent (translating natural language into deterministic read-only SQL queries executed directly against validated database rows) and a Grounded Gemini 2.5 Flash RAG Engine (retrieving verified report chunks via PostgreSQL full-text search with exact page and row citations). • SMOKEVISION Computer Vision Engine: An autonomous OpenCV surveillance engine that ingests spacecraft cabin video feeds, extracts smoke plume contours, calculates centroid drift velocity, computes calibrated Beer-Lambert optical depth, and integrates spatial Smoke Accumulation Dwell Tensors to identify cabin air stagnation pockets. • Interactive Simulation Lab: A real-time 2D physics sandbox with live fluid streamlines, FLIR thermal infrared false-color isotherms (200°C to 1400°C), gamified NASA flight officer missions, a custom rig builder with 1-click NASA ground truth benchmarking, and procedural Web Audio spaceflight acoustics.

2. WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

• Zero Hallucination (100% Citation Grounding): Solves the dangerous 38%+ hallucination rate of commercial LLMs by guaranteeing every flammability threshold is retrieved verbatim from real flight tests and every citation points to an authentic NASA Technical Memorandum. • Hands-Free Astronaut Voice Copilot: The CapCom Voice Assistant enables astronauts in pressurized gloves or spacesuits to query vital flammability limits and sensor data hands-free, featuring sub-second response times and aerospace text-to-speech normalization. • Early Stealth Fire & Smoke Warning: Detects ultrafine nanoscale pyrolysis aerosols (<100 nm) that evade commercial optical alarms, alerting flight controllers to electrical overheats 10–30 minutes earlier. • Scale Divergence Protection: Mathematically alerts mission planners when small glovebox duct tests (1–2 cm) diverge from full-scale spacecraft modules (0.4 m x 0.94 m), preventing catastrophic vehicle design errors.

3. WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT OF THE PROJECT?

Fire in human spaceflight is an existential threat with zero room for error. As human space exploration expands toward the Artemis Lunar Base, Lunar Gateway, commercial orbital stations (Axiom, Orbital Reef), and long-duration Mars transit vehicles, traditional ground-based fire safety protocols are no longer sufficient.

IGNIS-G provides flight controllers, habitat engineers, and astronaut crews with an authoritative, unified safety copilot. Its long-term impact is preventing catastrophic vehicle loss, optimizing life-support atmospheric compositions (O₂% vs pressure), and guiding the physical placement of next-generation multi-angle smoke sensors.

4. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE USED

• Backend & APIs: Python 3.14, FastAPI (REST API with 28 endpoints), Uvicorn. • Computer Vision & Scientific Computing: OpenCV, NumPy, SciPy (Eulerian vector fields, Beer-Lambert optics, particle morphology analysis). • AI & Language Models: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash, LangChain (create_sql_agent, SQLDatabaseToolkit), SQLAlchemy, Psycopg2. • Database & Cloud Storage: Supabase PostgreSQL with TSV full-text search (ts_rank), relational schema normalization, and evidence indexing. • Frontend & User Interface: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons. • Audio & Speech Engineering: Web Audio API (procedural synthesis of 55 Hz cabin hum, ignition whoosh, quench hiss, hazard warning alarms), W3C Web Speech API, MediaRecorder API with Gemini multimodal audio fallback. • Video Rendering: FFmpeg, PIL, Matplotlib. • Quality Assurance: 21/21 backend pytest tests passing, 16/16 frontend vitest tests passing, 0 TypeScript compile errors.

5. HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

• Epistemic Certainty Labeling: Rather than generating unconstrained text, the AI tags every output with mandatory certainty levels: [NASA observation], [Calculated result], [AI interpretation], [Research implication], or [Unknown]. • Multi-Sensory Digital Twin: Integrates live convective fluid streamlines and false-color FLIR thermal infrared cameras with procedural Web Audio spaceflight acoustics—creating an immersive flight controller training simulator with zero external audio assets. • Temporal Smoke Dwell Tensor: Creatively repurposes temporal computer vision integration to map air stagnation pockets in microgravity, generating actionable detector placement advisories for spacecraft cabins. • Gamified NASA Mission Deck: Turns complex microgravity transport equations into engaging, flight-certified safety challenges where researchers tune life-support parameters under real-time mission constraints.

6. WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

• The "Flag Over Fill" Principle: In life-support engineering, missing or unrecorded sensor channels must never be smoothed over or hallucinated. We designed the system to explicitly declare data gaps rather than fabricate answers. • Physical Boundary Invariance: We accounted for the fundamental physics divergence between Earth (1g buoyancy), the Moon (1/6g partial buoyancy), Mars (3/8g), and orbital freefall (0g diffusion dominance), enforcing physical gravity locks. • Astronaut Operational Realities: In an emergency, astronauts cannot type complex queries. We prioritized multimodal speech recognition with automatic silence dispatch and audio playback. • Hardware Agnosticism: We ensured the platform runs efficiently on standard modern hardware and web browsers without requiring expensive local GPU clusters.
